items.title: Henry "Pickle" Jackson Interview, 1961-08-09
items.q: In the old days, he had a swingin' jazz band. Papa Celestan always did have a swingin' jazz band... And Papa Celestan had one of the best swingin' bands in the South at that time.

ctx.x: I'm going to ask a little bit more about Celestan too. How did he play? I heard him in the late years, right before he died. He had a small band. In the old days, did he have a bigger band? Was that a sweet band too? Or what was it like?

In the old days, he had a swingin' jazz band. Papa Celestan always did have a swingin' jazz band. No, he didn't. He had a trumpet player by the name of Guy Kelly. He was playing in the band. Louis Barbaran was playing with his drummer, a feature drummer. Yeah. And Papa Celestan had one of the best swingin' bands in the South at that time. His band always was with swing. He had a lot of swing music. When Celestan played soft music or concert music, it's only when you request it. But he had some powerful men in his…

When he had people like Guy Kelly, somebody said he had shots with him for a while. How did he compare with the other trumpet? Was he as hot as the other fella or did he mostly take... Which one? Kelly? Yes. I mean, how was Papa Celestan? Did he see more people? Did he see more powerful than Guy Kelly? Oh. Or was Guy Kelly...
